paper-presentation.description: Paper Presentation is a technical event where participants present innovative ideas, research work, or technical concepts related to Computer Science and related domains. Teams will present their work using presentation slides and explain their idea, methodology, and impact. The event focuses on communication skills, technical knowledge, originality, and the ability to clearly explain complex concepts.

rounds.description: Participants submit their paper abstract before the event. Selected teams will be allowed to present their work during the presentation round.
Each team presents their paper using slides explaining the problem statement, methodology, implementation, and results.
Judges and audience may ask questions about the presented topic to test the participants’ understanding and clarity.

rules_and_regulations.domain: Topics must be related to Computer Science or related domains
rules_and_regulations.originality: Only original work is allowed. Plagiarism is strictly prohibited
rules_and_regulations.format: Presentation should be prepared using PowerPoint or similar presentation tools

judging_criteria.description: Understanding of the topic and depth of technical explanation
Creativity and originality of the idea presented
Clarity, confidence, and effectiveness in presenting the topic
Organization of slides, clarity of problem statement, and explanation of solution
Ability to answer questions confidently and accurately

ai-verse.description: Draft Edge is an individual design challenge that tests a participant’s ability to transform ideas into visually compelling designs. Through two creative rounds, participants demonstrate design thinking, creativity, and the ability to work within constraints while producing clean and impactful visuals.

rounds.description: Participants will be given a poorly designed visual such as a poster, banner, logo, or thumbnail. Their task is to analyze the flaws and redesign it into a visually appealing and well-structured design using Canva or similar tools.
Participants must create a minimal yet creative design based on a theme revealed on the spot. The design must follow specific constraints that test creativity, simplicity, and design discipline.

rules_and_regulations.tools: Participants must use Canva or similar design tools
rules_and_regulations.submission: Designs must be submitted within the given time
rules_and_regulations.fair_play: Any rule violation or late submission will lead to disqualification

judging_criteria.description: Innovative ideas and unique visual approach
Proper understanding and execution of the given challenge
Layout balance, color usage, and overall appeal
Smart and effective use of design tools and elements

code-volt.description: Duo Debug is a two-member team-based coding and debugging challenge that tests participants’ logical thinking, problem-solving ability, and teamwork. The event focuses on identifying errors, understanding program logic, and solving coding problems under time constraints. Through multiple rounds, participants will analyze outputs, debug broken code, and demonstrate individual coding skills while working as a team.

rounds.description: Each team will be given a set of 30 questions divided into three difficulty levels. The questions will test programming knowledge, logical reasoning, and output prediction skills. Teams must carefully analyze the questions and select the correct answers within the allotted time.

Participants will be provided with a broken code snippet along with the expected output. Teams must identify the errors in the program and correct them to produce the correct output. A total of five debugging problems will be given.

Two programming problems will be given. For a fixed time interval, team members will be separated and required to solve the problems individually. Communication between team members is strictly not allowed during this round, testing each participant’s independent coding ability.

rules_and_regulations.participation: Team event with exactly two members per team
rules_and_regulations.languages: Participants can use C, C++, Java, or Python
rules_and_regulations.communication: Discussion between team members is not allowed during the Blind Code round
rules_and_regulations.fair_play: Any malpractice or violation of rules will lead to immediate disqualification

judging_criteria.description: Correctness of answers and solutions provided by the team
Ability to identify and fix errors in the given code efficiently
Logical thinking and approach used to solve coding challenges
Completing the tasks correctly within the given time limit

prompt-paradox.description: Prompt Paradox is a cutting-edge AI challenge where participants use generative tools to solve mysteries, recreate visuals, and engage in high-stakes prompt engineering battles.

rounds.description: Participants must recreate a shown image using AI without using obvious or restricted keywords. Top 30% teams qualify.
Scan QR codes to unlock clues. Use AI tools to solve logic puzzles and progress. First 8 teams move to the final.
A two-phase battle. Defend your password with AI protection, then attempt to extract your opponent's password in limited attempts.

rules_and_regulations.devices: Computers provided, but personal devices are allowed
rules_and_regulations.timing: Strict adherence to round limits is mandatory
rules_and_regulations.judging: Judges' decisions are final and binding

judging_criteria.description: Effectiveness and efficiency of AI prompts used
Closeness of AI output to the original target image
Effectiveness of defense systems and attack patterns
Completion time for clue-based challenges

reels-and-rhythm.description: Fusionary is a fun non-technical guessing event where participants decode visual clues, music hints, and mixed image puzzles to identify songs or movies. Teams must observe carefully, connect the clues creatively, and guess the correct answer. The event tests creativity, quick thinking, and entertainment knowledge while encouraging teamwork and discussion.

rounds.description: Participants are given visual clues that represent lyrics or elements from a song. By interpreting the images and connecting them together, teams must identify the correct song.
Teams are shown a combination of images that hint at a particular movie. Participants must decode the meaning behind the images and guess the correct movie title.
A set of multiple images will be shown, but only 3 or 4 of them are relevant clues. Teams must identify the correct images, combine their meanings, and determine the corresponding movie or song.

rules_and_regulations.discussion: Teams can discuss among themselves before submitting the final answer
rules_and_regulations.answer_submission: Each team can submit only one final answer per question
rules_and_regulations.clue_format: Clues may be given in the form of images, symbols, or visual hints
rules_and_regulations.scoring: Points are awarded based on correct answers and speed of response

judging_criteria.description: Correctly identifying the movie or song from the given clues
Teams that answer correctly in less time receive higher points
Ability to interpret visual clues and connect them meaningfully
Effective teamwork and discussion while solving clues

wit-and-will.description: Clue Cracker is a team-based puzzle and guessing event where participants work together to decode clues and identify the correct answer. Teams discuss the hints and submit one final answer per question. Faster correct answers earn higher points, making teamwork, quick thinking, and logical reasoning essential.

rounds.description: Teams solve simple and common clues to get familiar with the game format and build confidence.
Questions are based on famous personalities, movies, and general knowledge where teams must decode clues to find the correct answer.
A special round where clues may be given through unique formats such as audio clips, visuals, or creative hint patterns.
The final round includes tricky logic-based clues with fewer hints, requiring teams to think quickly and answer fast.

rules_and_regulations.discussion: Teams can discuss among themselves before giving the final answer
rules_and_regulations.answer_submission: Each team can submit only one final answer per question
rules_and_regulations.scoring: Points are awarded based on accuracy and speed of answering

judging_criteria.description: Correctly identifying the answer from the clues
Faster correct answers earn higher points
Ability to analyze and connect clues effectively
Effective teamwork in discussing and solving clues
